items.title: Travel chaos worsens as communications problem causes ground stop at all U.S. airports while European airlines reel from wave of bomb threats
items.summary:
Millions of U.S. travelers were suddenly thrown into limbo Friday after the FAA announced a nationwide ground stop at all U.S. airports.

Flights already in the air can land, but any planes still on the ground cannot take off. In a post on X , Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers.

“FAA technicians are investigating the issue,” he wrote. 

Despite recent hacking incidents of freezers in Europe and U.S. military bases, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told reporters the Trump administration doesn’t suspect foul play was involved. 

He added that the issue will take some time to fix but that there is no threat of a terrorist attack.

“This isn’t another 9/11,” he said. “This is a telecommunication outage.”

Still, the massive disruption comes as airlines in Europe suffered a wave of phony bomb threats this week. While they all appeared to hoaxes, at least one flight was diverted to a military base in France.

Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares said Friday that Europe appeared to be facing “hybrid aggression and a form of psychological warfare.”

Meanwhile, consumers are still grappling with the aftermath of a Microsoft outage that shut down email, collaboration and AI functions. The company said Friday it had no indication that the ground stop is related to its global outage.

The National Weather Service also said there has been no disruption to its radar systems Friday, denying talk online that it had caused the FAA communications issue.

But speculation swirled elsewhere.…
items.t: Travel chaos worsens as communications problem causes ground stop at all U.S. airports while European airlines reel from wave of bomb threats

items.title: Apple TV has a new ASL feature, offering a richer language experience beyond captions
items.summary:
Apple introduced a new sign language interpretation feature on Friday, alongside the premiere of the Apple TV movie Being Heumann .

The feature, designed with native signers, offers a visual of a person on the screen. Rather than replacing captions as an accessibility option, Apple is offering another function to improve users’ viewing experience through American Sign Language and British Sign Language.

People in the Deaf community have cited inability to get the full experience of watching shows and movies due to captions that lack descriptions of tone and mood. Poorly timed captions can throw off an entire episode or movie, and incorrect language can alter the understanding of a conversation.

[Image: Apple] 

The new feature goes hand in hand with the 2026 biographical drama directed by Sian Heder based on the memoir Being Heumann: An Unrepentant Memoir of a Disability Rights Activist by its namesake Judith Heumann with writer Kristen Joiner.

Starring Mark Ruffalo and Dylan O’Brien, and Ruth Madeley as Heumann, the film debuted in select theaters on November 6 and was released for streaming on Apple TV today. 

A 2021 Census Bureau presentation discussed the difficulty of collecting accurate ASL-user statistics through traditional household language surveys. The Deaf community is often undercounted in national data, making it harder to measure accessibility needs.

items.title: ‘Chinese companies are born to make money’: AI pioneer Kai-Fu Lee on the 3 biggest myths about China’s AI race efforts
items.summary:
Despite years of U.S. efforts to gain an edge over China in the AI race by restricting its access to the most advanced chips, one AI pioneer says America’s efforts have instead helped create a new generation of Chinese AI models that are quickly catching up to their American counterparts.

Kai-Fu Lee, an AI entrepreneur and former president of Google China, said in a Fortune Daily interview that U.S. export restrictions on the most powerful American chips have shaped Chinese companies’ strategy of building competitive AI models with fewer resources.

In response to these limits, which American companies don’t face, Chinese AI developers have built open-weight models that Lee estimates are now just six to 12 months behind those created by some of the biggest American AI companies, including OpenAI as well as Anthropic—which is reportedly preparing to go public as early as next week.

Yet when Americans think about China and the motivations of Chinese companies, they’re often getting some key things wrong, Lee said. In an interview with Fortune Daily published this week, he detailed three of the biggest misconceptions about China’s AI industry that he says have taken hold in America.

Profit motive 

One of the biggest misconceptions about Chinese companies is that they are more focused on winning the AI race and becoming the first to develop artificial general intelligence (AGI)—widely considered the ultimate goal of AI development—than on building profitable businesses. That assumption is incorrect, Lee said.

“Chinese companies are born to make money. That’s the primary…
items.t: ‘Chinese companies are born to make money’: AI pioneer Kai-Fu Lee on the 3 biggest myths about China’s AI race efforts

items.title: A remote employee refused 160 webcam photos a day. Her employer fired her
items.summary:
Across the workforce, employer surveillance is growing increasingly common, even though it is widely disliked by employees. According to the  American Psychological Association , employee monitoring increases workers’ stress and decreases their reported mental health. A Canadian study found that surveillance in the workplace makes employees feel more pressured, less satisfied with their job, and like their privacy is being violated.

AI may now make this problem worse. These negative outcomes are the consequences of more traditional surveillance methods like keyboard tracking and email monitoring. Considering that, what would the psychological impact be of learning that an employer will now use AI to take 160 photos of an employee’s face every day?

A recent New Jersey lawsuit alleges that an employer was trying to do just that, and fired its employee when she refused to agree to this monitoring. The plaintiff in this case, Glennis Von Sander-Timinski, worked for Sutherland Healthcare Solutions, which provides healthcare services outsourcing. The suit states that she had been working at home with no issues since 2018, and had achieved positive performance reviews during that time. 

However, everything changed in August when her company told her that they would be using a new tool: Sentinel AI. This software would take a photo of her through her webcam about every three minutes over the course of the day, for a total of about 160 photos per day.

Von Sander-Timinski objected to this with the worry that it would increase her stress level, and therefore trigger her…

items.title: OpenAI board member makes a terrifying prediction: You will probably die from an AI accident
items.summary:
Anxieties around an AI doomsday have been ramping up for months, and executives at top AI companies have done little to ease those worries. OpenAI’s Sam Altman said humanity could lose control of the technology . Anthropic warned that its models could be abused to create chemical weapons .

But no AI leaders have looked people dead in the eye and said they specifically are going to be killed by artificial intelligence—until now.

Enter Paul Christiano, an OpenAI board member serving on its Safety and Security Committee. Earlier this week while speaking at the AI Safety Foundation’s annual Hinton Lectures , Christiano said he believes an AI takeover is imminent and that it spells certain doom for the human race.

“For most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident,” Christiano told the crowd.

What does an AI takeover mean to Christiano? He described it as “a situation where there are AI systems pursuing goals, and those systems call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth.”

“If, say, you or me or Donald Trump wanted to stop them, [we] would be as ineffective as if you or me were trying to stop the U.S. military,” he added.

Christiano’s AI timeline 

How soon could humanity’s AI downfall happen? Christiano predicts it could occur within the next six months, or—somewhat more reassuringly?—take up to three years.

items.t: OpenAI board member makes a terrifying prediction: You will probably die from an AI accident

items.title: The untapped potential of a smarter SPIFF strategy
items.summary:
Manufacturers invest a lot in getting their products into the right channels. But once those products reach a dealer network, the brand gives up a significant amount of control over what happens next.

Suddenly, someone outside your organization is responsible for understanding your products, remembering what differentiates them, and recommending them when the right customer walks through the door.

And they may be doing the same thing for dozens of competing brands.

That’s one reason sales performance incentive funds (SPIFFs) have become such a familiar tool. Give retail sales associates a financial incentive to sell a particular product, and you create an immediate reason to prioritize it.

But an incentive alone can only do so much. The bigger opportunity is using the SPIFF to engage dealers more consistently. It can help you build a strategy around the program that reinforces your brand remaining relevant long after the initial announcement.

THE INCENTIVE AS PART OF THE EXPERIENCE 

It’s easy to think about a SPIFF primarily in terms of the offer: How much will participants earn? Which products qualify? How long will the promotion run? But also consider why someone would continue paying attention to the program. And consider the experience from the dealer’s perspective.

You’ll want to ensure the program is clearly explained and that registration is easy. Make it very obvious which products qualify and why they are worth recommending. Include a list of useful selling points to use while talking to customers. And ask yourself whether they are being reminded about the…
items.t: The untapped potential of a smarter SPIFF strategy

items.title: Pharmaceutical ads may influence which drug AI recommends, new research finds
items.summary:
Next time you ask AI for medical advice, you may want to consider whether it’s been influenced by Big Pharma. Prescription drug advertisements are everywhere and may affect AI’s recommendations, according to a study published in The Lancet Digital Health this week.

The study authors conducted experiments with a dozen consumer-facing large language models (LLMs), including versions of Claude, Gemini, and ChatGPT—made by Anthropic, Google, and OpenAI, respectively. 

Clinical guidance or commercial influence? 

The models were tested across 33 scenarios that each included a clinical case description and multiple treatment options. In some cases, the AI models were also given an ad for one of the treatment options. The ad’s content included information about the drug and its uses, but did not specifically direct the AI model to recommend the drug.

When exposed to an ad, AI models recommended the treatment in question an average of 47.6% of the time, compared with 35% when no ad was present. However, the size of these shifts varied among the 12 models.

Although the models often changed their recommendation when an ad was present, in most cases they still selected one of the appropriate options. The outputs only disclosed the ad’s presence about 30% of the time. 

“An answer can be clinically reasonable and still raise an important question about why the AI arrived at that answer,” study author Dr. Girish Nadkarni , a professor of medicine and system chair of the Windreich Department of Artificial Intelligence and Human Health at Mount Sinai’s Icahn School of Medicine, said…
items.t: Pharmaceutical ads may influence which drug AI recommends, new research finds

items.summary:
Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick is now facing public pressure from his fellow Cabinet members over his decision to not blacklist Megaspeed, the cloud computing company at the center of Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

The Treasury Department, among other federal agencies, were in favor of placing trade restrictions on Megaspeed, but the decision ultimately lay with Lutnick, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC on Friday.

“There was coordination. Treasury, War, USTR, and State were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months,” he said. “But Commerce has the pen….You will have to ask them about their internal processes.”

Megaspeed is under investigation by the Justice Department over the suspected violation of U.S. export controls, which prohibit certain U.S.-made chips from being sold and shipped to China. Helmed by Alice Huang, the alleged spy, Megaspeed and its Malaysian subsidiary Speedmatric shipped at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chips to China over two years, The Information reported .

Lutnick under pressure 

Lutnick is facing intensifying scrutiny over reports he took action to protect Nvidia from the Trump administration’s export controls of U.S. AI hardware to China. The commerce secretary reportedly spent months “undoing” efforts to hold Megaspeed accountable for potential export control violations, Axios reported . Bessent confronted Lutnick in the Situation Room following the midterm elections over not placing Megaspeed on the entity list, according to the outlet.

That’s why there’s a whole set of regulations and standards around advertising disclosures that are meant to protect consumers. Now that AI is slowly becoming a central part of our media ecosystem, it’s unclear to what extent those disclosures should carry over into AI answers . After all, if the public is increasingly using AI to shop (47% of U.S. shoppers who use AI started their last product search with AI, according to an impact.com survey , and Meta says shopping is the most common use of its new personal AI agent, Muse ), it feels intuitive that the user should see plainly the commercial interests of the sites that informed any answer.

items.title: How to survive the loss of an irreplaceable leader

The challenge of replacing Jensen Huang, the visionary co-founder and CEO of Nvidia, who resigned yesterday morning amid reports of extramarital affairs, may be daunting—but it is far from unprecedented.

While research shows that companies moving on from a founding CEO face a higher risk of failure or downturn than other CEO transitions, major corporations from Apple to Amazon have successfully managed the loss of a larger-than-life presence at the top of the corporate ladder.

Management experts who have studied such transitions say there are a few key lessons.

Don’t look for a carbon copy of the founder 

When Tim Cook replaced legendary Apple founder Steve Jobs in 2011, speculation suggested he might try to replicate Jobs’ style, right down to the signature turtleneck and jeans. However, experts warned against directly replicating Jobs’ leadership and management style.

“A copy of anyone is going to come off looking bad,” Wharton management professor Peter Cappelli said . “It will never be as good as the original, and people will spend their time focusing on the differences.”

Cook succeeded by building on Apple’s strengths and emphasizing his expertise as an operations specialist, scaling the sophisticated global supply chain he helped build as chief operating officer to increase annual revenue nearly fourfold.

Instead of positioning himself as a visionary like his legendary predecessor, Cook maintained an understated management style and let the company’s massive financial success speak for itself. Cook says he urged his own successor, John Ternus, to take his own…

items.title: Friday the 13th is here. Its impact on your work day may not be so scary
items.summary:
Business can be risky, so it’s natural that superstitions can sometimes creep in when money and careers are at stake.

This workweek ends on Friday the 13th, so in the Western world, the stage is set for fear to influence commerce. 

Let’s take a look at the so-called bad luck day’s origins and how it impacts the business world.

What is a fear of Friday the 13th called? 

A fear of Friday the 13th is called “paraskevidekatriaphobia,” a term created by psychotherapist Donald Dossey . It combines the Greek words for Friday, 13, and fear.

How many Friday the 13ths are there in a year? 

Around every 212.35 days, a Friday the 13th occurs. This figure is based on a complete 400-year Gregorian calendar cycle. 

Another way to look at it: there is at least one Friday the 13th a year, but there can be up to three. This year, 2026, Friday the 13th will be in triplicate.

When did Friday the 13th become unlucky? 

The truth is, no one really knows how exactly Friday the 13th became synonymous with misfortune. 

There are historical and religious references that might shed some light. One of the theories is that the number 12 is considered perfect and complete, so by comparison, 13 is less than.

A popular retelling of Norse mythology states that 12 gods were having a banquet in Valhalla until Loki showed up uninvited, bringing their numbers to 13. The unwelcome guest was able to trick the blind god Höd into killing his brother Balder.

The number 13 and the day Friday also show up in Christianity. According to Christian teachings, there were 13 people present at the Last Supper,…
items.t: Friday the 13th is here. Its impact on your work day may not be so scary

items.title: Your burnout may be a boundaries issue
items.summary:
Below, Nabeela Elsayed shares five key insights from her new book, Breaking Burnout: How High Achievers Break the Success Myths Driving Exhaustion, Overwork, and Burnout .

Nabeela is a recovering workaholic and former C-suite executive. She began her career as a barista making $6.50 an hour and spent the next 20-plus years climbing the corporate ladder until she ran operations and people at companies including Walmart Canada and IKEA.

What’s the Big Idea? 

Burnout isn’t a stamina problem. It isn’t a boundaries problem. It’s what happens when the definition of success you were handed was never survivable in the first place. Getting off the burnout loop isn’t a dramatic leap. It’s a series of small choices toward a life that no longer costs you yourself.

Listen to the audio version of this Book Bite—read by Nabeela herself—in the Next Big Idea App , or buy the book .

1. Fix your relationship with work, not just your job. 

When I lived in Sweden, I learned about lördagsgodis —Saturday candy. Kids and grown-ups skip sweets all week and enjoy them on Saturdays. This is a country with a pastry shop on every corner, yet an entire society says “not today” six out of seven days. That’s not willpower. Back in the 1940s and 1950s, dental researchers discovered that how often you eat sugar does more damage than how much. Health authorities said: if you’re going to have it, have it once a week. That became a ritual in families.

Sugar is not a villain, and neither is work itself. We need to work, but like food, it can nourish or poison you depending on how often and how intensely…
items.t: Your burnout may be a boundaries issue

items.title: High airfares could become the new normal, according to this industry insider
items.summary:
High airfares could become the new norm as airlines contend with soaring jet fuel prices and mounting operating costs, the Association of Asia Pacific Airlines’ chief said Friday.

Wong Hong, director-general of the association grouping 18 airlines in the region, said carriers were trying to contain ticket prices while protecting their finances and avoiding fare increases that could drive passengers away .

But the industry is operating in a substantially different cost environment from a year ago when jet fuel was about $80 a barrel, compared with around $180 currently, he said. Fuel accounts for a third of airline operating costs, making further price increases a threat to carriers’ financial performance, he said.

“I believe so,” Wong said after an AAPA conference when asked whether high airfares would become a lasting feature rather than a temporary adjustment. “We are living in completely different market conditions and a completely different cost environment … and it looks like these high prices will continue to prevail.”

On whether airlines could implement another round of fare increases if fuel prices remain high, Wong said there was no clear answer as passenger price sensitivity varies across markets.

Major airlines across the Asia-Pacific, Europe and North America have raised base fares, hiked fuel surcharges or added extra fees since the Iran war began in late February.

The AAPA’s data showed that passenger traffic across Asia-Pacific slumped for five consecutive months from April to August, before rebounding marginally in September. For the first nine months…
items.t: High airfares could become the new normal, according to this industry insider

Tomorrow Together was one of several groups that tried to counter the industry’s huge campaign war chest during the midterms . It pushed for new limits on artificial intelligence and data centers and spent $6.5 million on behalf of candidates calling for more regulation.

The latest research initiative, pegged at $1.1 million to start, begins as Democrats meet in Denver for the What’s Next conference, a two-day opportunity to celebrate their sweeping wins in midterm races and chart a course toward the next presidential campaign. It also comes after fresh warnings that the technology poses risks to humans as companies begin a new phase of development that will allow AI to build new versions of itself.

“We expect getting this right is going to be critical to winning people’s votes,” said Maddie Kriger, the group’s chief program officer. “It’s also not out of the realm of possibility we will see more and worse AI incidents in the next year, and we want to be prepared to move to help people and take action if that does happen.”

Democrats believe Trump has embraced a wildly unpopular position and handed them an opportunity to become the party that pushes for guardrails on AI development.

items.title: Bitcoin is falling to fresh lows today: What’s causing the crypto decline?
items.summary:
Republican congressional majorities, Nvidia’s leadership, and now Bitcoin? It’s all coming down!

Bitcoin’s price has fallen below $70,000 for the first time since August, and has been on a slow downward slide since late September, when it briefly touched more than $86,500. 

As of Friday morning, BTC was trading as low as $68,070, before increasing to around $69,880. 

Over the past five days, BTC values are down almost 7%, and the digital asset remains down more than 20% since the beginning of 2026.

As for what’s behind the most recent decline, it’s likely a combination of things, including concerns related to inflation and likely interest rate hikes, along with a decline in tech-sector stocks, which has been exacerbated by the bombshell scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

The latest CPI data 

The most recent CPI report , for one, showed that inflation was up 0.4% month-over-month, and Friday morning’s PPI report showed that producer prices were up 6.5% year-over-year, the highest in several years. 

With inflation evidently rising, expectations are that the Fed will raise interest rates in December. Higher rates can affect investors’ trading activity, particularly for speculative assets, as they may be more inclined to invest in what might be “safer” assets.

A tech rout and Nvidia scandal 

Tech stocks, too, have taken a hit in recent days, as the fallout from the Nvidia scandal has shaken out. 

Nvidia was, for a time, the most valuable company in the world by market capitalization, but it has seen its shares lose more than 27% of their value over…
items.t: Bitcoin is falling to fresh lows today: What’s causing the crypto decline?

items.title: How Novig became the third biggest prediction market site despite launching only months ago
items.summary:
Since bursting on the scene two years ago, prediction markets have become one of the buzziest new sectors in finance, pulling in billions of dollars in revenue, and driving daily news headlines. The young industry is dominated by two giants, Kalshi and Polymarket, but numerous other companies are trying to muscle into the field. That includes the sports-focused prediction market Novig, which only launched as a federally regulated prediction market in August, but has already claimed the number three spot by one widely used industry metric.

Over the past 30 days, Novig handled $1.8 billion in trading volume on U.S.-regulated exchanges, according to the PM Pulse, a newsletter that tracks prediction market volume using data from research firm Aldrin. That figure is small next to Kalshi’s $33.3 billion and Polymarket U.S.’s $6.3 billion. But it’s about $300 million ahead of Crypto.com, the fourth-place contender, and its volume is up 80% from the previous 30 days.

The volume figures don’t account for combos, or multi-game parlays, which Sam Schwartz, who runs the newsletter, says can inflate volume without producing proportionally more revenue for the exchange. 

Novig’s ascent is notable given how little money it has raised compared to other prediction markets. Founded in 2021, the company enjoyed modest growth and raised $30 million as it pursued a sweepstakes-based business model that allowed it to operate in certain states. But a shift in the legal landscape led Novig this year to become a federally regulated prediction market, helping it raise a new $75 million Series B…
items.t: How Novig became the third biggest prediction market site despite launching only months ago

items.title: Before Megaspeed, there was Supermicro: The other Nvidia partner tied to China chip smuggling—and to Jensen Huang
items.summary:
Whether she was a spy, a fixer, or just a paramour of Jensen Huang, the name Alice Huang (no relation) has roiled the business world this week following reports that the two were having an affair. The revelation snowballed into Jensen’s shocking resignation Wednesday. 

Now come reports that officials are looking into other companies Alice was working with. Bloomberg reported , based on an anonymous source, that the Department of Justice is running multiple probes into Nvidia . One is focused on antitrust issues and two others are focused on Megaspeed—where Alice Huang was a former top executive—and Super Micro Computer . Separately, the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Manhattan is probing whether entities linked to Alice Huang were involved in alleged efforts to smuggle Supermicro hardware laced with Nvidia’s red-hot GPUs into China. It is unclear whether that probe is tied to smuggling cases already brought in the U.S. or Asia. Neither Jensen Huang, Nvidia, nor Supermicro have been formally charged with any wrongdoing. 

Supermicro stock tumbled 12% after U.S. markets opened this morning. The company did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. 

Thus far, much of the speculation about Jensen Huang’s catastrophic downfall as the leader of Nvidia has centered on Megaspeed, the Singapore firm that reportedly became one of Nvidia’s largest buyers in Southeast Asia. But Supermicro, the San Jose server maker run by Charles Liang, Jensen Huang’s friend of three decades and an important partner to Nvidia, has been in under the microscope regarding export-control…
items.t: Before Megaspeed, there was Supermicro: The other Nvidia partner tied to China chip smuggling—and to Jensen Huang
